clinical_category: Mannitol pharmacology - osmotic reduction of intracranial pressure and cerebral edema
blueprint_topic: Mechanism and therapeutic effect of osmotic therapy for increased intracranial pressure
stem: A nurse reviews the action of intravenous mannitol prescribed to reduce increased intracranial pressure. Which mechanism best explains this effect?

options.A: It increases extracellular and plasma osmotic pressure, moving intracellular water into the extracellular and vascular spaces
options.B: It directly repairs the structural brain lesion responsible for the increased intracranial pressure
options.C: It lowers plasma osmolarity so water shifts from the vascular space into brain tissue
options.D: It primarily blocks cerebrospinal-fluid production through carbonic-anhydrase inhibition

rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed prescribing information states that intravenous mannitol increases the osmotic pressure of the plasma and extracellular space, inducing movement of intracellular water into the extracellular and vascular spaces. The label directly identifies this action as underlying mannitol's role in reducing intracranial pressure and intracranial edema. B is incorrect because mannitol is a physiologic treatment for pressure/edema rather than a repair of the underlying structural cause. C reverses the osmotic gradient. D describes a different pharmacologic mechanism and is not the labeled mechanism of mannitol.
educational_objective: Recognize that intravenous mannitol reduces intracranial pressure by increasing extracellular/plasma osmotic pressure and shifting intracellular water into extracellular and vascular compartments.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label updated 2026-05; current label accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: DailyMed current MANNITOL Injection label → Indications and Usage: reduction of intracranial pressure and treatment of cerebral edema. Section 12.1 'Mechanism of Action': intravenous mannitol increases extracellular/plasma osmotic pressure, inducing movement of intracellular water to extracellular and vascular spaces; this action underlies reduction of intracranial pressure and intracranial edema.
source_claim_supported: The current official mannitol label directly supports increased extracellular/plasma osmotic pressure with movement of intracellular water into extracellular/vascular compartments as the mechanism that reduces intracranial pressure and edema.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests medication mechanism, therapeutic effect, and safe understanding of osmotic therapy for acute neurologic complications.
correction_summary: Substantive refinement. The generic FDA label landing page was replaced with a current specific DailyMed label and exact Section 12.1 locator. The final item preserves the directly supported osmotic mechanism while removing the source rationale's unneeded claim that mannitol is necessarily a temporizing measure in every clinical context.
audit_findings: The original generic FDA URL failed the exact-locator requirement.
Current DailyMed Section 12.1 directly supports the osmotic movement of intracellular water into extracellular and vascular spaces and links this mechanism to reduced intracranial pressure and edema.
The source's broad statement that mannitol is a temporizing measure was not required for the construct and was removed rather than generalized.
Distractors represent reverse osmotic movement, direct lesion repair, and an unrelated carbonic-anhydrase mechanism; none is defensible for mannitol.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible mechanism, no unsupported dose/osmolality target, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
